thread:
nidhi: Quick sync — exploring privacy-forward metering. Can we avoid shipping raw token text into the billing stream but still support accurate token counts, attribution, and audit replay when necessary?

sam: Clarify: you want to strip token text before it hits the central stream/ingest? :thinking_face: 

nidhi: Yes. Concept: only emit numeric token_count + a deterministic per-tenant digest/fingerprint instead of full transcripts. Keep provenance (request_id, model, route) intact.

mike: That lowers PII footprint. For audits/regressions where we might need to replay prompts, how do we restore transcripts?

nidhi: Two approaches: (A) persist encrypted transcripts to a KMS-backed object store with tight access controls and TTL; or (B) keep only irreversible digests and use an escrowed key for time-limited re-identification.

jess: B sounds risky from compliance/legal perspective unless the escrow is extremely controlled. A is operationally cleaner.

alex: Performance/cost: we're worried about KMS per-request overhead. If we go with encrypted objects, we should use per-tenant DEKs cached per process and only call KMS on rotate/write, not per request.

sam: For billing you mostly need counts per tenant and per-window. Could the edge calculate token_count and drop token text before sending to the collector? That sidesteps central transcript handling.

mike: Attribution across services requires a stable join key. Something like HMAC(token_text, tenant_salt) yields stable, irreversible IDs for tokens. But if tenant_salt is constant, there is a fingerprinting risk if the attacker has many inputs.
nidhi: Threat model: internal engineers with broader data access, legal requests, and accidental leakage. Goal: minimize plaintext retention and require explicit, auditable steps to access decrypted data.

jess: Proposal sketch: - Edge emits token_count and token_digest = HMAC(SALT, firstN_hash || lastN_hash || total_len) - Stream consumes token_count + digest + provenance - Transcripts encrypted with per-tenant DEK, stored in audit-bucket with IAM guards + 30-day default TTL - Audit flow requires ticket + manager approval to decrypt (KMS unwrap + audit log entry)

sam: That keeps KMS ops low (object write -> wrap once). But some workflows (long-running evals) may want >30d retention. Make it opt-in per-customer under enterprise contract.

alex: Implementation detail: digests must be deterministic and well-documented (concatenate token-hashes with separators) so separate systems can recompute for joins. Also plan salt-rotation: keep last N salts for a join window; rotating removes linkability over time.

mike: Billing aggregation path can ignore any digest — we only need counts. So split responsibilities: billing path = low-latency counts-only; audit path = digest + encrypted transcripts with stricter controls and slower ingestion if necessary.

nidhi: Streaming responses pose edge cases: tokens arrive incrementally. Edge needs to emit interim deltas and a final_count flag on stream close. If the edge fails, server-side counter must be able to produce counts without raw tokens present. Need handshake to mark which side counted.

alex: Suggest an event field counted_by: [edge|server] and final_count boolean to reconcile. Collector dedupes by request_id.

jess: Auditing UX: auditor requests decrypt via UI; request ties to ticket/approver; decrypt attempts are immutably logged with approver identity; returned transcript may be redacted depending on policy.

sam: Customers will ask how we ensure counts weren't altered if we don't keep plaintext. Consider publishing signed per-tenant aggregates (daily merkle/signed checkpoints) so customers can verify counts.

nidhi: Agreed. Signed daily aggregates containing token_count and checksums of digest sets gives tamper-evidence without exposing content.

mike: PoC notes: - Edge: add HMAC and token_count emission (low CPU) - Collector: accept counts+digest, support counted_by and final_count flags - Storage: store compressed aggregates + encrypted object references - Audit service: approval workflow + KMS decrypt path - Monitoring: track decrypt frequency, KMS errors, long-retention opt-ins

alex: Performance watch: computing first/last token-hashes at edge adds CPU. We should benchmark on small edge instances and track cost for bursty clients. Also consider a fast non-crypto hash for internal summaries and HMAC for any joinable identifiers.

jess: Security/Compliance tasks: define key rotation policy, least-priv IAM for audit decrypt, separation of duties, and legal review for escrow patterns. Include these in RFC.

sam: Can we prototype quickly? PoC: edge SDK flag to emit digest+counts, collector schema change for compatibility, encryptor service and audit UI stub. 2-week spike.

nidhi: PoC goals: zero extra per-request KMS calls, measurable reduction in plaintext retention, working decrypt audit path, clear perf impact numbers.

alex: I'll draft a test plan: unit tests for deterministic digest, sandbox ingest with counted_by scenarios, bulk decrypt CLI for audit flow, cost/latency bench harness.

mike: I'll build a small CLI for decrypt/replay tests that simulates the approval flow and records audit logs.

jess: I'll own sec review and produce a threat model doc and a ticket for key-management policy.

infra-bot: Deploy note: PoC branch created at github.com/redwood/ingest/tree/feature/privacy-metering-poc and deployed to sandbox. :rocket: 

nidhi: Thanks team. Let's meet Thu 10:30am to review PoC acceptance criteria. I'll author a short RFC outlining two main options and recommend counts-only billing + encrypted, auditable transcripts as the default. :+1:

sam: Add a migration plan for analytics teams and external partners who rely on full transcripts today.

mike: Also flag any partners consuming raw streams; we need a transition/contract addendum.

jess: Filing: creating SEC-OPS ticket for KMS/key management and ENG ticket for PoC tasks.

nidhi: Closing thread for now. Comments welcome on the RFC once I post it. :slightly_smiling_face:
